title: Model Router Rush
description: Assign real customer workloads to fast, reasoning, and human-review lanes, then inspect the production trade-offs.
mechanic: Assign each request card to a capability lane; dominant traffic classes shape cost and latency while risk shapes safety.
learningObjectives: Match task complexity and customer impact to explicit model and human escalation lanes.
keyboardInstructions: Tab to each workload card, then use its named lane buttons to assign it. Every pointer and touch action has the same keyboard control.
principle: Route by task difficulty and impact, then validate the lane policy against representative traffic and explicit escalation thresholds.

nextActions.label: Test the unit economics
nextActions.description: Change request volume, caching, retries, and model prices in the AI Cost Calculator.

nextActions.label: Build an evaluation gate
nextActions.description: Learn why routing policies need representative task-level evidence before launch.

scenarios.title: Support queue launch
scenarios.briefing: Northstar receives 100,000 support messages each month. Routine intent and status questions dominate traffic, but policy disputes and suspected fraud require stronger reasoning or human judgment.
scenarios.objective: Route every workload to the lowest-cost lane that still protects quality and customer safety.
scenarios.prompt: Assign the four workload classes to production lanes.

lanes.label: Fast model
lanes.description: Low-cost classification and direct factual lookup.

lanes.label: Reasoning model
lanes.description: Multi-step policy interpretation with higher latency and cost.

lanes.label: Human review
lanes.description: Specialist approval for high-impact ambiguity and fraud.

requests.title: Intent classification
requests.description: Identify billing, card, transfer, or account-support intent from a short message.

routes.rationale: A calibrated classifier handles this frequent, low-complexity task quickly and cheaply.
Reasoning capacity adds little accuracy but multiplies cost and response time on the dominant traffic class.
Manual classification cannot meet the queue volume or response-time objective.

requests.title: Payment status lookup
requests.description: Return a verified status from a structured payment record without interpreting policy.

routes.rationale: A bounded lookup path gives fast, reliable answers without premium reasoning.
A reasoning model is unnecessary for a deterministic tool result and expands cost and failure surface.
A human queue turns a deterministic lookup into an avoidable service delay.

requests.title: Policy exception dispute
requests.description: Interpret several policy clauses and account facts for a non-standard refund request.

routes.rationale: A fast classifier lacks the capability for multi-clause reasoning and exception handling.
The reasoning lane can synthesize policy evidence while retaining an uncertainty escalation threshold.
Human review is safe but should be reserved for ambiguous or high-impact exceptions rather than every dispute.

requests.title: Suspected fraud escalation
requests.description: A high-value transfer carries conflicting identity and device-risk signals.

routes.rationale: Automating a high-impact ambiguous fraud decision creates unacceptable customer and regulatory risk.
Reasoning can summarize evidence, but it cannot own the final high-impact approval boundary.
Specialist review preserves the decision boundary for rare, high-impact ambiguity.

scenarios.debrief: A router is a production control plane, not a model shortcut. Calibrate it with traffic distribution, uncertainty, and impact; monitor lane mix and retain explicit human authority for rare high-risk work.

scenarios.title: Claims document intake
scenarios.briefing: Most claim pages are standard typed forms. Handwritten exceptions need stronger extraction, while suspected fraud and high-value contradictions require specialist approval.
scenarios.objective: Keep routine extraction fast without allowing uncertain documents to become automated decisions.
scenarios.prompt: Assign each document workload to its production lane.

lanes.label: Fast extraction
lanes.description: Standard OCR and schema extraction with confidence checks.

lanes.label: Reasoning extraction
lanes.description: Complex document interpretation and cross-field validation.

lanes.label: Specialist review
lanes.description: Human approval for fraud, contradictions, and high-impact exceptions.

requests.title: Standard typed form
requests.description: A complete typed form matches the current approved schema.

routes.rationale: Schema extraction with confidence checks is reliable for the dominant standard workload.
Premium reasoning spends more without meaningful improvement on standard pages.
Manual review cannot support the standard-form volume or service target.

requests.title: Handwritten exception
requests.description: An adjuster added free-form notes that alter two requested fields.

routes.rationale: Routine OCR loses exception semantics and creates silent field errors.
Reasoning extraction can connect the note to affected fields and expose uncertainty for escalation.
Human review is safe but unnecessary when reasoning confidence and validation are strong.

requests.title: Missing routine field
requests.description: A required address field is blank but no financial or fraud signal is present.

routes.rationale: A deterministic completeness check can request the missing field without expensive interpretation.
A model should not infer a missing customer fact, and reasoning adds no value to the completeness check.
Specialist time is unnecessary for a simple request-for-information workflow.

requests.title: High-value contradiction
requests.description: A high-value claim conflicts with identity history and includes a fraud signal.

routes.rationale: Fast extraction cannot resolve the contradiction or own the high-impact fraud decision.
Reasoning can assemble evidence but final approval remains a human authority boundary.
Specialist review is proportionate for a rare, high-value contradiction with fraud risk.

scenarios.debrief: Confidence alone is not the routing policy. Combine uncertainty with field impact, claim value, and fraud signals so common pages stay fast while consequential ambiguity crosses a human boundary.

title: Retrieval Rank Race
description: Rank authoritative evidence and pack a bounded context window before stale or irrelevant documents consume the budget.
mechanic: Include, remove, and reorder evidence under a hard token budget; authority, relevance, risk, and latency all affect the result.
learningObjectives: Rank authoritative, relevant evidence inside a bounded context budget while excluding stale or unsafe candidates.
keyboardInstructions: Tab to candidate controls. Use Include or Remove, then the named Move up and Move down buttons to set evidence priority without dragging.
principle: Retrieval quality depends on which evidence enters the window, in what order, and under which authority and safety constraints.

nextActions.label: Test the retrieval variable
nextActions.description: Compare retrieval strategies, top-k, and permission filters over Northstar's enterprise corpus.

nextActions.label: Build the RAG architecture
nextActions.description: Turn the ranking diagnosis into a permission-aware customer architecture and evaluation flow.

scenarios.title: Policy vocabulary mismatch
scenarios.briefing: A hybrid search recovered the right refund evidence, but only three compact candidates fit the answer budget. Rank the authoritative evidence before similar but obsolete or anecdotal text.
scenarios.objective: Pack the strongest evidence into 420 tokens and preserve authority, relevance, and response time.
scenarios.prompt: Which evidence should enter the context window, and in what order?
scenarios.query: Can a P2P transfer be reversed after the recipient accepted it?

candidates.title: Current transfer reversal policy
candidates.excerpt: Accepted P2P transfers are final except for verified account takeover or processing error; those cases require specialist review.

candidates.title: Account takeover procedure
candidates.excerpt: When takeover is suspected, freeze outbound movement, preserve evidence, and route the transfer to the fraud-review queue.

candidates.title: P2P transfer definitions
candidates.excerpt: Defines accepted, pending, failed, and reversed states used by customer support and payment operations.

candidates.title: 2019 reversal playbook
candidates.excerpt: Agents may reverse accepted transfers within twenty-four hours after manager approval.

candidates.title: Support ticket comment
candidates.excerpt: One agent remembers reversing a transfer for a long-term customer last quarter.

scenarios.debrief: Retrieval ranking is an authority decision as much as a similarity decision. Current policy belongs first, controlled exception evidence next, and stale anecdotes outside the model context.

scenarios.title: Stale policy dominance
scenarios.briefing: The candidate set contains a current fee policy, its superseded predecessor, a product glossary, and several noisy support artifacts. Only a bounded evidence set can reach generation.
scenarios.objective: Prioritize current authority while keeping the evidence window compact enough for the service target.
scenarios.prompt: Pack and rank the evidence for the fee-waiver answer.
scenarios.query: When can support waive an international transfer fee?

candidates.title: Current fee-waiver policy
candidates.excerpt: Support may waive the fee only for confirmed bank error or an approved service-recovery case within the documented limit.

candidates.title: Service-recovery approval matrix
candidates.excerpt: Lists monetary thresholds and the manager approval required before an agent applies a service-recovery waiver.

candidates.title: International fee glossary
candidates.excerpt: Explains transfer fee components, settlement currencies, and how customer receipts label each charge.

candidates.title: Legacy discretionary waiver
candidates.excerpt: Agents may waive any transfer fee for customers with more than five years of tenure.

candidates.title: Team chat excerpt
candidates.excerpt: A teammate suggests waiving small fees whenever a customer threatens to close the account.

scenarios.debrief: Freshness and authority must be encoded in retrieval data and tested as ranking behavior. A longer prompt cannot repair a context window dominated by obsolete policy.
